# Vendored third-party code

Other authors' code, vendored in-tree — there is no package manager — and compiled into **both** app targets: `taglib/`, `PINCache/`, `PINOperation/`, `r8brain/`, `dr_mp3/`, `dr_flac/`, `dr_wav/`, `ogg/`, `vorbis/`. `Sparkle/` is the exception: prebuilt, and only in the macOS direct download (below). **Do not restyle it.** Regenerate with `xcodegen generate` after changing the file set. Edit `project.yml` when a file needs special flags or an exclusion.

Every component must be listed in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md` at the repo root with the license it is used under. **TagLib is dual-licensed (LGPL 2.1 or MPL 1.1) and Vibe elects MPL 1.1**. Read that file before touching `taglib/`.

- **taglib** (a subset of TagLib 2.3.2, `toolkit/taglib.h`'s version) extracts audio metadata. Only the formats the app plays are vendored: `mpeg/` and ID3, `mp4/`, `flac/`, `riff/`, `ogg/` with its `vorbis/` and `opus/` files, plus the APE *tag* machinery MPEG files need and `ogg/xiphcomment` for FLAC and Ogg comments. Not Ogg FLAC, which the player refuses, and nothing for CAF or W64, which TagLib cannot read: their facts come from CoreAudio (`Audio/Metadata/AGENTS.md`). `TagLib::FileRef` is deliberately unused, since its detection references every format parser. The `TagLibAudioFile` factory (`Audio/Metadata/TagLibAudioFile.mm`) stands in for it. It mirrors FileRef's extension-then-content-sniff detection for the supported formats. An update re-checks it against `fileref.cpp`. Four packaging edits: `toolkit/tlist.h` and `toolkit/tmap.h` carry their `.tcc` files pasted in where each was included, `toolkit/tstring.cpp` includes `utf8-cpp.checked.h` for `<utf8.h>`, and `taglib_config.h` defines `TAGLIB_WITH_APE`, without which `MPEG::File` compiles its APE reading out (`testMP3WithAnAPETag`). When updating, re-copy the subset, re-apply those edits and let the linker report anything new; 2.3 added the MP4 chapter and STEM files, which `MP4::File` now references. Re-count the files carrying both license notices in `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`.
- **PINCache** and **PINOperation** provide disk and memory caching for metadata and waveform data. `PINDiskCache.m` is excluded from the recursive `ThirdParty` entry and re-added with a per-file `-fobjc-arc-exceptions` flag, as the pod's ARC-exception-safe subspec did. `make check-layout` whitelists that exclude, along with the `.xcprivacy`, `.txt` and `LICENSE.MPL` ones that keep license and privacy files out of the bundle — this directory is the only place file-level excludes are allowed at all. **`PINDiskCache.m` is modified**, each change marked `Vibe:` so `grep -rn 'Vibe:' PINCache PINOperation` lists them for re-applying after an update: the access-count xattr is neither written per hit nor read per file at launch unless eviction is least-frequently-used; a hit re-dates its file, and the date the eviction sorts by, only once that date is a day old; outside a TTL cache a write removes no age-limit xattr, since none is ever set; a hit reads its file outside the cache's one lock, as it already deserialized, so concurrent hits run concurrently; and an automatic trim cuts to 90% of the byte limit, so a full cache sorts its entries once per tenth of the limit written rather than on every write. **`PINOperationQueue.m` is modified once**, marked the same way. Its semaphore queue runs at utility QoS. Without that, a user-initiated enqueue waits on a semaphore that utility operations signal. The Thread Performance Checker flags that priority inversion.

- **r8brain** (r8brain-free-src, upstream commit `9e73d2dd`) is the voice bus's resampler (`Audio/AudioResampler.mm`). It is header-only apart from the two files `project.yml` excludes and re-adds with their own flags, `DLL/r8bsrc.cpp` (upstream's C entry points, where every template is instantiated) and `fft/pffft_double.c`: `-O3` in every configuration, since at `-O0` it would cost many times its optimized self and a Debug build is where its quality and cost tests run; `-DR8BSRC_DECL=` (upstream's switch from a DLL to an object file); `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`, the README's speed setting (double-precision PFFFT at Ooura's accuracy) — its other, `R8B_EXTFFT`, costs more than it saves at the 1% transition band `Audio/AudioResampler.mm` uses, so it is off (`docs/audio-quality.md`); and `PFFFT_ENABLE_NEON`.

  **TRAP: PFFFT's NEON path is opt-in, and `-w` hides the `#pragma message` that says so** — without the macro arm64 silently uses the scalar fallback. x86_64 selects SSE2 by itself. Check with `clang -arch arm64 -fsyntax-only fft/pffft_double.c` plus the flags, which prints the backend chosen. `-w` silences the vendored C's warnings. Every file that includes an r8brain header must see the same `R8B_*` macros, so nothing but `r8bsrc.cpp` includes them.

  Upstream's `LICENSE` is vendored as `LICENSE.txt`, and the `.inc` filter tables are excluded, so neither is bundled. Only what those two files compile is vendored (checked with `clang -H` for arm64 and x86_64): not upstream's `r8butil.h`, the single-precision `pffft.c`, the Ooura `fft4g.h` (unused under `R8B_PFFFT_DOUBLE`), the Windows DLL builds, `bench/` or `other/`. When updating, re-copy the same set and re-run that check.
- **dr_mp3** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_mp3 0.7.4) is `AudioFileHandle`'s default MPEG decoder (MP1, MP2, MP3), Apple's the alternative in the mac's Settings > Advanced (`docs/audio-quality.md`). Only its frame decoder (`drmp3dec_*`) is called: CoreAudio's parser still frames the packets. `dr_mp3.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, and defines `DR_MP3_FLOAT_OUTPUT` itself (its comment says why). `project.yml` excludes it and re-adds it with `-O3` in every configuration, for r8brain's reason, and `-w`. The license texts are at the end of the header.

  **`dr_mp3.h` is modified** on the `vibe-mp3-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`. The frame decoder fixes cover MPEG-1 Layer III's private bits being read as the first granule's scfsi, and the 8 kHz row of `g_scf_mixed` (MPEG 2.5 mixed blocks). That row uses long bands 0–5 and short bands 3–12. Upstream's row reordered 600 lines, 24 floats past the granule, and scaled three bands by an earlier granule's scalefactors. The branch also carries upstream PRs for the `drmp3` API that Vibe does not call.

  When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`, whose `testDrMP3DecodesWhatAppleRoundsTo16Bits` holds the decode to Apple's, and whose `testDrMP3IgnoresPrivateBits` and `testDrMP3DecodesMixedBlocksAt8kHzAsFFmpegDoes` fail on upstream's copy.
- **dr_flac** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_flac 0.13.4) is `AudioFileHandle`'s FLAC decoder (`docs/audio-quality.md`). It reads the stream itself, through the handle's descriptor, after CoreAudio's parser has answered the file's facts. `dr_flac.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, with neither stdio nor Ogg, and builds with dr_mp3's flags.

  **`dr_flac.h` is modified** on the `vibe-flac-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`.

  Format and seek fixes cover an ID3v2 prefix, empty first residual partitions, stale seek tables, invalid frame headers, and a binary search that keeps the target bracketed. Damaged frames stay in the timeline as silence. A truncated frame still ends the stream. A seek past a truncated stream lands at its end. The decoder supports 32-bit streams and their 33-bit stereo side channel. An unknown (0) length does not clamp seeks.

  Damage handling covers undefined arithmetic in side channels and metadata, invalid residual partitions, bad Ogg CRCs, stale samples after failed frames, fixed-block frame numbering, false or missed sync codes, bit-stream position and exhaustion, and unreachable seekpoints. Decode and seek share the damaged-frame walk. They fill a gap only before a valid frame, resume a failed frame's search from its header, and distinguish truncation by exhausted input. A failed seek leaves the decoder at the first frame. Binary-search probes are bounded. Skipping and decoding both reject a negative LPC shift.

  Unknown-length streams use `drflac__find_unknown_total_pcm_frame_count` at open. It finds the end of the last valid frame by searching backward from the tail. The search window doubles after a miss. This supplies the nonzero length `AudioPlayer` requires and permits bisection seeks. A STREAMINFO allowing no block is not searched.

  Rice partition orders above 8 are accepted in decoding, skipping and the 33-bit side channel. Only the streamable subset limits them (RFC 9639 sections 7 and 9.2.7). The seek fast path keeps its distance at 64 bits. A jump of 2^32 PCM frames or more must not wrap into the current frame.

  Performance changes include CRC-16 eight bytes at a time, NEON and SSE2 f32 conversions that agree with scalar results outside the bit depth, and Vibe's NEON residual decoder. `drflac_read_pcm_frames_f32_planar` writes each channel straight to its own buffer. Separate stereo conversions keep planar reads from slowing interleaved reads. Measurements are in `docs/audio-quality.md`. `dr_flac.c` keeps NEON enabled.

  When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`: `testDrFLACDecodesWhatTheFileHolds`, `testDrFLACSurvivesWhatDamagesFiles` and `testDrFLACSeeksFurtherThanThirtyTwoBitsOfFrames` fail on upstream's copy. They check what decodes and seeks deliver, and what seeks cost only near a garbage seekpoint, so a copy that seeks slowly again, as upstream's search could for seconds on a long file, passes them.
- **dr_wav** (dr_libs, upstream commit `dfe83776`, dr_wav 0.14.6-dev) is `AudioFileHandle`'s WAV, W64, RF64 and AIFF(-C) decoder of integer and float PCM, A-law, mu-law and ADPCM (`docs/audio-quality.md`), offered no file whose parser names another container (`VibeDrWAVReadsContainer`). It reads the stream itself, through the handle's descriptor and the same callbacks as dr_flac, after CoreAudio's parser has answered the file's facts. `dr_wav.c` is ours, the one implementation unit, without stdio, and builds with dr_mp3's flags; `DRWAV_MAX_SAMPLE_RATE` stays upstream's 384 kHz, so a faster file is Apple's.

  **`dr_wav.h` is modified** on the `vibe-wav-fixes` branch of `cmicali/dr_libs`.

  Fixes: an AIFF's SSND offset and block size fields counted as audio (forward seeks landed late in any AIFF with a chunk after SSND); AIFF-C A-law and mu-law bytes shifted as signed 8-bit samples; unsigned 8-bit silence converted to 1/255; a COMM, fact or ds64 count trusted past the data; PCM seeks placed from the frame count less the bytes remaining, and a seek past 2 GB stepping in `INT_MAX` bytes, a partial frame each; data sizes of 0, 0xFFFFFFFF or wrapped past 4 GB (the 0xFFFFFFFF recount read from the end of the file); an IMA ADPCM block cut short counted by bytes, not groups, and an MS ADPCM one by a whole header however little of it was there; COMM chunks of 23 bytes, odd size or more than 18; a fmt chunk after the data; four chunk sizes that hung the open, and a long seek with no `onTell`, found by fuzzing; the MS ADPCM sample update overflowing; a damaged ADPCM block ending the stream or dropping out of the timeline, now silence in its place; W64 padding; the MS ADPCM fact count never used; the AIFF rate's 80-bit conversion overflowing; WAV ADPCM block sizes that cannot decode; and ADPCM data shorter than one block header, whose count came from a fact chunk past the data.

  MS ADPCM uses the stream's coefficient table instead of the built-in seven pairs. The decoder accepts up to the 256 pairs a block's predictor can name, as CoreAudio does. A table cut short of its count, or one of no pairs, is refused. MS ADPCM prediction has one implementation.

  Added formats are AIFF-C twos, in24, in32, 42ni, 23ni and ima4. The ima4 decoder carries its predictor across packets as CoreAudio does. It saves decoder state every 64 packets for exact seeks. PCM, float and G.711 read into the f32 output and convert in place with NEON or SSE2 at scalar accuracy. `drwav_read_pcm_frames_f32_planar` converts stereo straight into one buffer per channel with NEON. ADPCM reads ahead 16 KB at a time and seeks from the block holding the target.

  When updating, diff the copy against upstream's `dfe83776`, re-apply what upstream has not merged, and run `make test-audio`: `testDrWAVDecodesAsAppleDoes` and `testDrWAVSurvivesWhatDamagesFiles` fail on upstream's copy.

- **libvorbis** (`vorbis/`, upstream commit `1b75110b` of xiph/vorbis, after 1.3.7) and **libogg** (`ogg/`, 1.3.6, commit `be05b13e` of xiph/ogg) are `AudioFileHandle`'s Ogg Vorbis decoder on both platforms (`Audio/AGENTS.md`). Both are BSD-licensed and unmodified. libvorbis's master is used for the decoder fixes made since its last release, among them a use-after-free in `ov_pcm_page_seek` and large stack allocations. Only the decoder is vendored: `include/vorbis/codec.h` and `vorbisfile.h`, and the twenty `lib/` files and nineteen headers that link without the encoder's entry points. `bitrate.c`, `envelope.c` and `psy.c` are encoder code that `block.c` references, so they link but never run. libogg's `ogg.h`, `os_types.h`, framing and bit reader sit flat in `ogg/`, so `<ogg/ogg.h>` resolves through the `ThirdParty` search path. Its `config_types.h` is not needed, since `os_types.h` has an Apple branch. Each `COPYING` is vendored as `LICENSE.txt`.

  **TRAP: none of their headers may join the project.** Xcode's headermap finds a header by its name from any target, and libvorbis's `vorbisfile.h` would answer for TagLib's. So both directories are excluded from the recursive entry, and only their `.c` files are added back (`includes: ["*.c"]`, `project.yml`), with dr_flac's flags. **TRAP: the search path finds TagLib's `vorbis/vorbisfile.h` first** (`taglib/ogg` precedes `ThirdParty`). libvorbis's own files find theirs through `-iquote`, and `AudioFileHandleInternal.h` names it by its path in the tree, `vorbis/include/vorbis/vorbisfile.h`.

  When updating, copy the same file set from upstream, check that it still links, and run `make test-audio`. `testOggVorbisDecodesWhatTheFileHolds` and the CoreAudio fuzz family read every Vorbis fixture through it.

- **Sparkle** (2.10.0, from the release tarball `Sparkle-2.10.0.tar.xz`, SHA-256 `c2bf58aa8387266ac179357b1415d6f2635f044da8be41042af32425dae6da0c`, GitHub's own digest for the asset) is the direct download's updater (`Mac/App/AGENTS.md`, Updates). It is vendored prebuilt, not as source: `Sparkle.framework` as shipped, its `LICENSE` as `LICENSE.txt`, and `bin/sign_update` and `bin/generate_keys`, which `release.sh` and `github-release.sh` run. Both app targets' `ThirdParty` entries exclude `Sparkle/**`, and the macOS target re-adds the framework as an embedded dependency, unlinked in the `AppStore` configuration. Its dSYMs, test app and other tools are not vendored. When updating, replace those four with the new tarball's, record its version and digest here, read its changelog for a raised minimum macOS (2.10 needs 12.0), and run the local update test: two Debug builds with a throwaway key (`VIBE_SPARKLE_PUBLIC_KEY=` on the build, `sign_update -f <key file>`), a feed on `localhost`, and the older one launched with `--update-feed`. It must install the newer one from inside the sandbox.

**The dr_libs fixes live as commit series on the `cmicali/dr_libs` fork**: `vibe-mp3-fixes`, `vibe-flac-fixes`, and `vibe-wav-fixes`. Each is based on upstream's `dfe83776`, with one change per commit. Keep each vendored header equal to its branch's tip. Change a decoder on its branch in a clone of the fork. Never change only the vendored copy or use a scratch worktree for the fork. Commit and push the branch before copying the header into `Vibe/ThirdParty/`. Then run `make test-audio`. Re-vendoring from upstream requires diffing against `dfe83776` and re-applying fixes upstream has not merged. The tests named above fail on upstream's copies.

`make analyze` ignores findings in `ThirdParty/`. Vendored decoders are still exercised by `make test-audio`.

Framework-style imports such as `<PINCache/...>` resolve through the shared `vibe-header-paths` setting group in `project.yml`, which both app targets use so a second platform cannot drift from the first.
